edges.mechanism: Self-relevance supplies top-down priority signals that can bias selective attention toward personally significant information.
boundary_conditions: Self-relevance is context and identity dependent.
Bottom-up salience can compete with self-relevance.
transport_limits: Neurocognitive review does not justify a universal marketing effect size.

edges.mechanism: Affective goodness/badness evaluations provide a rapid informational input that can be used as an affect heuristic in judgment.
boundary_conditions: Affect is useful only when treated as diagnostic of the target.
transport_limits: No claim that affect dominates all decisions.

edges.mechanism: Promotion/prevention motivational orientation moderates persuasive response when message features are motivationally matched or mismatched.
boundary_conditions: Matching effects vary across motive types and outcomes.
transport_limits: Do not equate personalization with motivational matching.

edges.mechanism: Salient social identities and accommodation goals can bias register/style choices and interpretation of socially indexed language.
boundary_conditions: Language identities are fluid and interaction-specific.
transport_limits: Sociolinguistic identity is not a fixed persona label.

edges.mechanism: Evaluative lexical polarity helps construct the gain/loss meaning of a decision description and can thereby shift risky choice framing.
boundary_conditions: Reference-point and outcome-salience mechanisms must be distinguished.
transport_limits: Evidence is strongest for controlled risky-choice framing tasks.

edges.mechanism: Syntactic/structural complexity can alter the amount and character of message processing, thereby changing conditions for elaboration.
boundary_conditions: Complexity can increase effort or impair comprehension depending on ability and motivation.
Sentence length is not equivalent to syntactic complexity.
transport_limits: No universal claim that simpler syntax persuades better.
